narrative.overview:
The site is a working LED information board, the kind that hangs in Saudi mosques, schools and office lobbies: a black-green acrylic face, a visible grid of unlit dots, a thin aluminium frame, and dot-matrix lettering that lights up to say something. Projects are the board's rows, each with an honest status light, and the real application screens light up on a screen beside the board. Whatever the board displays (names, headlines, figures, dates, the ticker) is set in the LED face; whatever is read or operated is set in a calm sans that carries Arabic and Latin as one family.

The two themes are the same object in two lights. Lit, the default, is the board switched on at night. Print is the board printed as a timetable card in daylight: white stock, darkened inks and a pale halftone dot. Visitors choose Auto, Print or Lit (تلقائي / مطبوع / مضاء); Auto follows the device.

Density is that of a departures board: tight rows, small muted labels and large lit values, with generous space between boards. Colour is rationed to three LED inks with fixed jobs, and only one amber plate is ever inverted on a screen. English and Arabic are full peers with native right-to-left layout. Motion is the board relighting through its own dot grid, and it stands down completely under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dot-field surfaces inside thin frame rings; nothing casts a blurred shadow.
Three LED inks with fixed jobs: amber acts, green is live or public, red carries figures.
Lit (560) and unlit (260) static Handjet instances for display; Readex Pro for reading.
2px corners on every rectangle; circles only for LED dots.
Status drawn by pattern on one five-stage lifecycle, always with words, colour only reinforcing.
Relight motion on a shared 6px dot pitch, with full reduced-motion fallbacks.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Amber means you can act; green means live or public; red carries figures, dates and the ticker. An ink never borrows another's job, none is used as decoration, and product colours appear only inside real captures.

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: A screen has at most one inverted amber plate. Where a board is present it is the lit row, and the action beside the board is outlined; a filled amber action appears only on screens with no lit row (a case study's project-site action, the 404 return action).

rules.name: The Unlit Rule
rules.body: An unconfirmed fact is shown, never hidden or guessed: it is set in unlit LED (weight 260, Dim Ink) and says "to be confirmed". A lit value is a verified value.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Handjet ships only as lit (560) and unlit (260) static files. Never ask the LED face for another weight, and never load the variable Handjet: its dot contours are too slow to interpolate on phones.

rules.name: The Display/Read Rule
rules.body: Handjet LED is for what the board displays: names, headlines, figures, dates, ticker lines, the brand lockup and tool names. Readex Pro is for anything read in sentences and for control labels (actions, nav, filters, the language switch).

rules.name: The Native Script Rule
rules.body: Arabic LED gets its own sizes, 10 to 20% below the Latin ones (board headline clamp(36px, 3.9vw, 54px), section titles clamp(32px, 3.6vw, 48px), row names clamp(22px, 2.1vw, 28px)), with letter-spacing 0 and line-height 1.15. Latin names inside Arabic lines are isolated left-to-right and kept unbroken. The English name in the lockup is set in capitals.

rules.name: The Repack Rule
rules.body: Narrow screens repack rows and grids instead of shrinking type: LED sizes stay fluid while rows restack.

rules.name: The Logical Rule
rules.body: Layout uses logical properties and inline-start/end throughout. Both languages keep the same order, and directional icons mirror under right-to-left.

rules.name: The Frame Ring Rule
rules.body: Every box-shadow is a ring with zero offset and zero blur. If something needs to stand forward, frame it; do not float it.

rules.name: The Dot Field Rule
rules.body: Board-like surfaces carry the dot grid token: Unlit Dot lamps of 1.15px radius, softening to 1.65px, on a 6px pitch, laid over Board Face or Bezel Band. Prose areas, the masthead and the footer stay plain.

rules.name: The Two Pixel Rule
rules.body: Corners are 2px, or 1px when nested. Nothing is a pill, and nothing is round unless it is a dot.

rules.name: The Pattern First Rule
rules.body: Every status reads from shape alone (filled, half or ring; lit, unlit or ringed pip) and always comes with words. Colour only reinforces.

rules.name: The Relight Rule
rules.body: Content never slides, bounces or scales into place. It lights, through the dot mask on the 6px pitch or by fading in once decoded. The ticker is the only continuous movement, and it can always be paused.

dos: Do build new surfaces from the board kit: the dot field over Board Face inside the board bezel for major panels, a 1px Aluminium Frame for plates and cards.
Do keep Signal Amber for things that respond to input, including the 2px focus outline at 3px offset and text selection.
Do keep one inverted amber plate per screen: outline actions beside a board, filled actions only where no row is lit.
Do show every status with pips or glyph pattern plus words, on the five-stage lifecycle.
Do set unconfirmed facts in unlit LED (260, Dim Ink) with "to be confirmed".
Do use only the lit (560) and unlit (260) Handjet instances for display, and Readex Pro for prose and control labels.
Do give Arabic LED its own smaller sizes with letter-spacing 0 and line-height 1.15, and isolate Latin runs left-to-right.
Do keep 44px targets for actions, text actions, nav, the language switch and footer links, and at least 40px for in-board controls.
Do mount only real captures or source-project assets on plates, with honest captions.
Do ship a reduced-motion fallback with any new relight or crawl.
donts: Don't add soft, offset or blurred shadows; frames are zero-blur rings and 1px borders.
Don't introduce a fourth ink or decorative colour gradients, or let amber, green and red stand in for one another.
Don't light a value that is not verified, or fill an unknown with a placeholder figure.
Don't round rectangles beyond 2px or make pills; circles are for dots only.
Don't set paragraphs or control labels in the LED face, or request Handjet weights other than 560 and 260.
Don't shrink type to fit narrow screens; repack rows and grids instead.
Don't use AI-generated, rendered or invented imagery.
Don't move content into place with slides, bounces or scale-ins.
